# Idea

<a id="01-lead"></a>
### 01-lead

Ord
: 1

Kind
: lead

Text
: Your phone is the most personal computer you own, and the one you control least. You cannot see what it runs. You cannot change it. And when its maker stops sending updates - usually after a few years - a machine that works perfectly well becomes a risk you carry in your pocket.


<a id="02-problem"></a>
### 02-problem

Ord
: 2

Kind
: problem

Heading
: Two doors, both locked

Text
: Almost every phone in the world runs one of two systems, each owned by one company. The hardware underneath could run something else: Linux, the free system that already runs most of the world's servers.

But a phone that runs Linux today can rarely be someone's only phone. The call drops, the camera stays dark, the battery does not last the day. And every phone model needs its own patient work, done by a handful of volunteers, mostly started again from nothing for each device.


<a id="03-idea"></a>
### 03-idea

Ord
: 3

Kind
: idea

Heading
: Make the work ordinary, and make the truth visible

Text
: Two things, together.

**A conveyor.** A lab of tools and written procedures, so that bringing Linux to a phone is the same known steps every time - flash it, check it, listen to it, fix what fails, send the fix where everyone gets it - done by a person or by an agent, and never leaving the phone broken.

**An honest picture.** Every thing a phone must do, set against every system that could do it: what works, what half works, what is missing - and, shown plainly, what nobody has measured yet.


<a id="04-picture"></a>
### 04-picture

Ord
: 4

Kind
: picture

Heading
: A workshop, not a miracle

Text
: One brilliant mechanic can fix one car. A workshop with the right lifts and gauges and written procedures fixes any car - and the next mechanic starts where the last one stopped.


<a id="05-idea"></a>
### 05-idea

Ord
: 5

Kind
: idea

Heading
: As good as Android - and counted

Text
: The aim is plain: a phone running Linux that an ordinary person could use as their only phone, and not feel they gave something up. We count towards it one feature at a time, and a feature counts only when something has shown that it works.


<a id="06-limit"></a>
### 06-limit

Ord
: 6

Kind
: limit

Heading
: What is still hard

Text
: Some parts of a phone are kept shut by their makers - the modem, the camera, the secure chip - and can only be worked with from outside. Banking and payments depend on decisions that are not ours. There is one phone in the lab so far. And for Linux phones as a whole, most of the picture still reads: not known yet.

### 07-start

Ord
: 7

Kind

Heading
: Where it stands

Text
: One phone, a Xiaomi POCO X3 NFC, sits in the lab. It can be flashed to a known state by one command, and it is checked after every start. Sound plays from both of its speakers. Its microphone and its calls are still ahead. The picture lists forty-six things a phone does, across seven systems.
